phases.name: Discovery
phases.description: Audit current state, identify gaps, map tech debt, assess readiness for v1.0.0

findings.finding: Clean layered architecture (shared → domain → application → infrastructure → app). Crate boundaries are well-defined with zero circular dependencies.
44 tweaks defined but only 32 registered in make_all_tweaks(). 12 tweaks exist as files but are not wired into the engine.
findings.fix: Register all remaining tweaks in commands.rs make_all_tweaks()

findings.finding: DebloatEngine still relies heavily on PowerShell (Get-AppxPackage pipelines, registry scripts). Violates project Rule #5 (DEBLOAT IS NATIVE).
findings.fix: Replace with windows-rs COM PackageManager + native WinRegistryProvider writes

findings.finding: Snapshots are SQLite-only. No file-based JSON payload with verification. No export/import functionality.
MetricsCollector uses PDH for CPU/RAM/Disk/Network. Missing GPU metrics, temperature readings, and system overview (WMI).
findings.fix: Add SystemOverviewCollector using WMI for CPU name, GPU, motherboard, OS build, uptime

findings.finding: Vanilla JS frontend is functional but basic. No circular progress indicators, sparkline charts, or theme toggle. Uses polling (5s setInterval) instead of Tauri event emission.
findings.fix: Add SVG-based circular progress, canvas sparklines, CSS theme switching, Tauri app.emit() for push updates

findings.finding: toggle_game_mode command exists but uses raw reg.exe/powercfg calls instead of native windows-rs. No per-game profiles or process detection.
findings.fix: Refactor to native Windows API, add GameProfile entity, process detection via CreateToolhelp32Snapshot

findings.finding: clean_recycle_bin uses PowerShell Clear-RecycleBin. Error reporting tracks but doesn't prevent partial failures.
findings.fix: Replace with SHEmptyRecycleBinW Windows API call

findings.finding: CI runs cargo check and cargo test. Missing cargo tauri build step, Inno Setup packaging, and release artifact upload.
findings.fix: Add cargo-tauri build job, Inno Setup step, GitHub release artifact upload

findings.finding: iced_test/ crate is orphaned dead code. Not in workspace. AGENTS.md references Iced but project uses Tauri.
findings.fix: Removed iced_test/ directory from repo, AGENTS.md correctly describes Tauri v2

findings.finding: No Windows Restore Point integration before batch operations. No SRSetRestorePoint FFI call.
findings.fix: Add RestorePointService with SRSetRestorePointW FFI, call before all batch operations

findings.finding: Settings page shows version and database path but lacks theme toggle, safety level selector, backup retention config, and notification preferences.
findings.fix: Add settings table to SQLite, wire to frontend with all config options

phases.name: Competitor Analysis
phases.description: Analyze top Windows optimization tools (CTT WinUtil, O&O ShutUp10++, Sophia Script, WinHance, BloatyNosy, Optimizer) to identify feature gaps and competitive advantages

competitors.name: Chris Titus Tech WinUtil
strengths: All-in-one: debloat + install + ISO builder + troubleshooting
Win11 Creator for custom debloated ISO
weaknesses: Not a native binary (script trust concerns)
features_to_borrow: Troubleshooting quick fixes (SFC, DISM, network reset)

competitors.name: O&O ShutUp10++
strengths: Regularly updated for new Windows builds

competitors.name: Sophia Script / SophiApp
weaknesses: May trigger endpoint protection false positives

competitors.name: BloatyNosy (ThisIsWin11/WinPilot)
weaknesses: Was pulled from Microsoft Store previously

zingerboost_unique_advantages: Native Rust binary (10x lighter than Electron/.NET)
Snapshot rollback system (only optimizer with guaranteed undo)
zingerboost_gaps_vs_competitors: No ISO builder (WinUtil has Win11 Creator)
No troubleshooting quick fixes (WinUtil has SFC/DISM/network reset)
No community plugin system (BloatyNosy has this)
Fewer tweaks than Sophia Script (44 vs 150+)
No hardware info display (Optimizer has this)
market_differentiators: Only Rust-native Windows optimizer with snapshot rollback
Lightest binary size in category (<30MB target)
Enterprise-grade architecture with clean crate boundaries

phases.name: Critic Review
phases.description: Critical review of the generated roadmap for feasibility, risks, gaps, and recommendations

strengths: Roadmap is grounded in actual codebase analysis (not hypothetical)
Prioritization aligns with existing tech debt severity ratings
Acceptance criteria are specific and testable
Competitor analysis identifies concrete gaps to fill
Preserves project's unique advantages (Rust native, snapshot rollback, open source)
Version targets are realistic given feature scope
All features respect the locked tech stack (Rule #1-12)

risks_and_mitigations.risk: F1.1 DebloatEngine refactor is high-risk and could break existing functionality
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Keep PowerShell as fallback during transition. Add integration tests for each bloatware target. Test on clean Windows 11 VM before merging.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: F4.2 Process detection adds polling overhead and may miss short-lived processes
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Use WMI event subscription (Win32_ProcessStartTrace) instead of polling for more reliable detection. Add debounce to prevent rapid apply/revert cycles.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: F8.1 zb_tray crate adds significant complexity (new binary, IPC, shared state)
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Consider using Tauri's built-in system tray API in zb_app first before creating a separate crate. Only split if main app needs to run independently.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: F5.1 GPU temperature via WMI may not work on all hardware
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Use multiple fallback strategies: WMI → PDH → OpenHardwareMonitorLib DLL. Gracefully degrade with 'N/A' if no source available.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Feature creep: 28 features across 11 epics may be too ambitious for v1.0.0
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Strictly scope v1.0.0 to E1-E4 only. Move E5-E11 to v1.1.0/v1.2.0. Focus on core stability and UI polish first.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: No automated UI testing strategy for Tauri + vanilla JS frontend
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Add Playwright or Spectron for E2E testing of frontend. At minimum, add manual test checklist for each release.

recommendations.recommendation: Scope v1.0.0 to E1 + E2 + E3 only (Core Stability + UI Enhancement + Presets). This delivers the most value with manageable risk.
Defer zb_tray (E8) to v1.2.0. Use Tauri's built-in system tray in zb_app for basic tray functionality in v1.0.0 instead of a separate crate.
Add a 'Copilot Removal' tweak (F10.4) to the v0.0.7 release. This is a high-demand feature in 2026 and competitors are already addressing it.
Implement F1.4 (File-Based Snapshots) before F3.2 (Preset Apply). Preset apply depends on reliable snapshot creation for rollback safety.
Add a 'Troubleshooting' tab (like WinUtil's Config tab) with SFC, DISM, network reset, and Windows Update repair. This is a frequently-used feature that competitors offer.
Create a 'Removed Apps' log in SQLite to track what was debloated. Enable reinstallation via winget. This addresses the 'no undo for debloat' gap.
Add a 'Before/After' benchmark feature. Measure boot time, RAM usage, and process count before and after applying tweaks. Provides tangible proof of optimization.
Consider adding a 'Portable Mode' build option (like Optimizer). Some users prefer running from USB without installation. Can be achieved by storing data in app directory instead of %LOCALAPPDATA%.

overall_assessment.critical_path: E1 (Core Stability) → E2 (UI/UX) → E3 (Presets) → E4 (Game Mode) → E9+E11 (Release)
key_success_factors: Maintain strict scope discipline per version
Test DebloatEngine refactor thoroughly on clean VMs
Keep snapshot rollback as the #1 safety feature
Preserve Rust native advantage (no Electron/PowerShell regression)
Community engagement for feedback and testing
